string-array.name: changelog_v37
string-array.item: Dragging the strip past A or Z keeps the letters under your finger instead of stopping at the edge, and dragging up past A no longer closes the list: Settings › A–Z strip › Strip follows past the ends — off by default.
Past Z the list jumps to its end, so the last row can be reached from the strip too.
The warning before freezing a folder now names only the apps that freeze will actually touch, so a folder that merely holds Settings no longer warns about it.

string-array.name: changelog_v36
string-array.item: Frozen apps can be drawn in greyscale as well as faded, so they stand out in bright daylight: Settings › Appearance › Frozen app look.
After a restart the firewall reads the device back instead of trusting its record, so a cut-off the phone forgot is made again.
A pause the system lifts by itself — the “unpause and open” dialog — is noticed now, so an app that is already open is not left offline.

string-array.name: changelog_v35
string-array.item: Protect essential apps is a row in Settings › App freezing now, not the last switch in the automatic-freezing dialog, so the settings search finds it while freezing is on.
A pinned freeze shortcut whose app has left the freeze list says the shortcut is no longer available instead of doing nothing.
Add a home screen shortcut is only offered for apps that are on the freeze list.

string-array.name: changelog_v34
string-array.item: A narrow half cell keeps the look it had before: a folder\'s name under its icon, an app\'s beside it. The setting can still ask for either.
Freeze all from the home menu or the corner gesture now asks before it takes a package that keeps the phone working, as the freeze screen already does.
Freeze all now names every app on the list that could leave the phone unusable, including ones with no icon on the home screen.

string-array.name: changelog_v33
string-array.item: In two columns, a narrow half cell can put the name under its icon instead of beside it. The app list gives names two lines before an ellipsis.
The freeze list keeps one row per app, so an app that registers two launcher activities no longer closes it.
Protect essential apps now covers the app that answers calls and the SMS app, and its description says what turning it off means.
Freezing the screen, Settings, the installer or the permission layer asks first, and rules, the tile, the corner gesture and broadcasts leave them alone.
The corner button can start the phone\'s voice assistant listening.
The A-Z strip no longer comes up squashed after the launcher restarts.

string-array.name: changelog_v32
string-array.item: Folders sit in their column again in the two-column layout. A folder shares its row with an app, and the chevron is dropped in that cell so the name has room. One that holds a widget or Now Playing keeps the whole row, because it opens in place.
The app list follows. With two columns on, a folder sits beside an app of its own letter instead of alone on a line.
A wave reach slider under the A-Z strip settings pulls the wave and its letter bubble in from the edge, so they stop covering app names, or pushes them out.
A widget that scrolls takes its own up-and-down swipes. The home screen no longer opens the list or the shade underneath it, and a slow scroll no longer pops the widget\'s menu.
A folder near the bottom slides into view while it opens, so a finger already on its way down lands on the app it was aimed at.
The search keyboard comes up while the list is still sliding in, not a moment after it settles.
Top bars stay clear of the camera cutout on phones whose status bar is hidden.
The clock can size the widget to what it is showing, and each clock row gets its own space above. Both live in Edit layout.
The A-Z strip settings now say where the strip\'s range is dragged.
External control: the broadcast command shown with the token now names the receiver. Android 8 and later drop a broadcast without a component, so sending commands did nothing before.

string-array.name: changelog_v31
string-array.item: Per-app firewall: cut the apps you choose off the internet while everything else stays online. Each app follows freeze, stays blocked or stays online, protected apps and the dialer are never touched, and an app installed while the firewall is on joins the list.

The firewall has a page of its own: search, system apps, a filter per state, and counts for offline, waiting and unconfirmed apps. Android drops these rules on reboot, so they are written again at start-up.

The freeze list is now one table: every app on the phone, the method for each and whether it is frozen. The method is set per app (Stop, Suspend, Disable, Hide), and a comparison page says what each one survives.

Permanent freeze replaces the old pin: a permanent app stays frozen through Unfreeze all, a folder release and the automatic thaw. A handover exit or the app\'s own switch still thaws it, and the list can show only permanent entries.
Pick a default method for new entries, add or remove several apps at once from the selection bar, and switch freezing itself off from the freeze page.
The dialer and the system-critical packages can no longer be frozen by accident; the row says why it is held.
Thawing an app that an older version suspended under another identity now works: the suspension is lifted under the name the system recorded, not only under the current one.

Folders: the name keeps to one line and takes the whole row in the two-column layout, app names get two lines, and a folder may be left unnamed. Opening a folder in two columns shows its members in a popup.
A locked app stays suspended, not merely hidden, so Settings cannot put it back on the launcher.
Uninstalling the app that lends the freeze channel, Shizuku or the root manager, warns that frozen apps could no longer be thawed.
Developer options: screen scale, to try the layout at a phone size other than this one.

string-array.name: changelog_v30
string-array.item: Edge gestures can be turned off: the A–Z strip dialog now has a side row (left, right, both) and a gestures row (left, right, both, off), and Off also stops a tap on the edge from opening the app list.
Entries on the freeze list can be pinned: a pinned app stays frozen through Unfreeze all, a folder release, a handover exit or an automatic thaw. Freezing and thawing a single app is unchanged.
Freeze or thaw one app inside an open folder: long-press a member and use the same menu as the app list.
Freezing a folder now touches only the apps already on the freeze list; the rest are left alone and the toast says how many were skipped.
Short screens: the automatic freezing window, Select all, Invert, the system-app switch and the freeze-method dialog scroll to the bottom.
Settings shows every option at once. The advanced switch is gone, the cards are grouped by what they change, and the A–Z strip has a card of its own.
The A–Z strip can sit on the left, the right or both sides, and the home screen and app list move aside to make room for it.
Bulk runs say what really happened: Unfreeze all counts only what stayed frozen, a folder release counts only what it thawed, and a partly applied import says how many entries it could not take.
A state that cannot be read is no longer counted as frozen or thawed, an uninstalled app no longer counts as a failure, and a damaged settings table is refused instead of overwritten.

string-array.name: changelog_v29
string-array.item: Freezing has a screen of its own: Stop, Suspend, Disable and Hide each get a tab, and a table says which channel can run which.
Freeze without root or Shizuku: make Deluge the device owner, or let Dhizuku lend its owner rights, and Suspend or Hide works from the phone alone.
Long-press a folder to freeze or thaw every app inside it at once.
Drive it from a script: broadcasts and deluge:// links freeze or thaw one app or the whole list, so Tasker and shortcuts can do it too.
Sleep rules: freeze or wake the list by Wi-Fi, headphones, a time window, charging or battery level.
Daily limits: set how many times an app may open per day; once it is reached the app is frozen until tomorrow.
Not opened in 90 days: a one-tap list of apps you have forgotten; add them to the freeze list from there.
Focus mode: long-press an app to hand the phone over showing only that app; unlocking brings the rest back.
Handover mode and two new tiles: hand the phone over with everything frozen, and lock the private space from the shade.
Encrypted backups: export with a password; a wrong password on import leaves the current setup untouched.
Notification colour is now a choice, and apps paused in a work profile grey out like suspended ones.
Smaller fixes: settings survive a damaged preferences file, and app locks are rebuilt after one.

string-array.name: changelog_v28
string-array.item: Folders can hold the Now Playing card: long-press a folder and pick \"Add Now Playing\". The card opens with the folder, even when nothing is playing yet.
The quick-launch swipes now reach the bottom of the home screen, even when favorites fill it.
Buttons inside an open folder no longer lose their taps to the edge strip that opens the app list.
With the status bar peek set to 0 seconds, the bar hides at once, including when you come back from an app.
All home widgets can be stacked, each keeping its own height.
The A-Z strip can move as a bell or as a ripple, with speed, damping and stiffness sliders.
The letter bubble on the A-Z strip can be rounded, circular, square or hidden.
Folder members show their newest notifications, and a sideways swipe clears a line.
The wallpaper dim setting now says that it dims the wallpaper.

string-array.name: changelog_v27
string-array.item: Notification text under favorites shows up to three notifications per app, newest first. Tap one to open that notification, and set its own text size.
A dot beside the name when icons are hidden and the app has notifications.
On a Japanese phone, app names file under kana rows, and kanji names under one row of their own.

The private space padlock ends the app list; its menu installs apps into the space and opens the space\'s settings. Locking an app offers the same path: create the space, install it there, remove the copy outside.
Widgets can live inside folders, above the apps, with their own height and settings menu.
Folders in the app list have a long-press menu: manage apps, add to or remove from the home screen, delete.
The clock widget follows the launcher\'s font.
A notification panel pulled down from the home screen: every notification with its buttons and a reply box.
Favorite rules show or hide favorites by Wi-Fi, time of day, headphones or a daily open limit.
The freeze screen explains Android 15\'s private space when the phone has it.
App lock now covers notifications, shortcuts, the now-playing card, the camera button and widgets: each asks for your screen lock before it opens the app.
A locked app no longer leaves a freeze record behind that could keep it disabled after unlocking, and the freeze list survives reinstalling Deluge.
The freeze method picker shows counts for installed apps, and favorites can be hidden from their long-press menu.
The app-lock timeout now says how long an unlocked app stays open before it locks again.
All 8 languages complete.

string-array.name: changelog_v26
string-array.item: Protected apps, on by default: the current keyboard, the home app, accessibility services, Shizuku and root managers are never frozen.
Work profile and private space apps can be frozen too, each profile kept apart even when the package name is the same.
One tile in the shade freezes or thaws the whole list.
Any app on the list can pin its own switch to the home screen.
The freeze list exports to a file and imports on another phone.
Freezing is faster: one pass reads every app state, and through Shizuku each app is a single binder call.
Automatic freezing comes back after a reboot instead of waiting for the launcher to be opened.
Apps the system parked as disabled until used, common on Samsung phones, open normally again instead of failing to unfreeze.
Hidden apps keep their icons after a reboot, and unpausing an app restores its background settings.
All 8 languages complete.

string-array.name: changelog_v25
string-array.item: When another app opens a paused app, the system dialog now offers Unpause and open instead of a dead end. Apps paused by an earlier version get that button on their own.
Notification text on rows: the newest notification shows under the app name in favorites. Off by default.
Apps open out of their icon and shrink back into it on a gesture back.
The A-Z strip setting now measures the whole reach from the screen edge, and defaults to 40 dp instead of 56, so it no longer covers the leftmost icons.
Shizuku is recognised by its API rather than by a package name, so Shizuku-Next, Shevery and other compatible managers work too.
Importing settings is bounded: 1 MB per file, 64 KB per string, capped lists and range-checked numbers, so a hand-edited backup can no longer crash the app.
Copying a crash log replaces packages from other profiles with [private].
All 8 languages complete.

string-array.name: changelog_v24
string-array.item: Freeze apps with root or Shizuku: Stop, Suspend, Disable or Hide, one tab per method, each with what it costs. The screen says whether root (and which root: Magisk, KernelSU, APatch) or Shizuku is answering.

Freezing has triggers, not a switch: Freeze all, the corner button, a shortcut on the launcher\'s own icon, or automatic freezing a while after the screen goes off. The automatic run leaves the app on screen, apps with notifications and a phone on a charger alone.
System apps stay out of the freeze list until you turn them on. Select all and invert fill or empty the list in one go, and both long-press menus freeze or unfreeze a single app.
Settings is a two-column grid, with the search box still over every row.
Export settings now covers every setting, the language, and re-pins the shortcuts it names. Freeze state and update-check records stay on the device.
Distinct icons for each direction: a snowflake to freeze and a sun to unfreeze, a closed lock to lock and an open shackle to unlock. Uninstall is red in both menus.
Widgets refresh when their app freezes or unfreezes, and a frozen widget is never cleaned away.
Freeze commands are batched through one shell, so a long list no longer waits a command at a time.
Reconcile clears a frozen mark the system no longer reports, instead of leaving an app greyed out forever.
All 8 languages complete.

string-array.name: changelog_v23
string-array.item: A folder that expands near the bottom scrolls its apps into view instead of leaving the last rows off-screen.
Settings → About can check the release page for a newer version. It reads, and sends nothing.
Edit layout: the grab handle sits clear of the system back gesture, so a reorder drag starts on a gesture-navigated phone, and a drag the system interrupts keeps the order you dragged it to.
The A-Z strip: the letter under your finger is the one that lights, and letters hidden by the corner button leave a gap instead of squeezing the rest away from your finger.
The clock, weather and agenda widget\'s settings open at once: apps, calendar and battery are read off the main thread, once, not every frame.
Pausing or resuming an app no longer empties the icon cache; backups leave out the icon cache and the notification counts.
Settings sliders follow your finger without writing to storage on every frame.
The flashlight switch keeps its state after you leave the home screen, and the clock widget no longer asks for a 30-minute idle wake-up it never uses.
All 11 languages complete.

string-array.name: changelog_v22
string-array.item: Corner button: press gives, hold slides up to run; tap and slide each pick from nine actions; drag it anywhere in edit layout.
Swipes under the favorites offer the same nine actions, one set per side.
Auto-dark follows custom night hours you set.
Each gesture binds its own app or shortcut, adds do-nothing, and backing out of a picker changes nothing.
Swipe-down shade restored; weather survives reboot; widget counts stay true.
Backups leave the corner button\'s private app out and round-trip the language.
App-list scrubbing lands at once; icon warmup shares cores with the finger.
Fifteen-plus audit fixes: torch loop, empty-folder text, folder dimming, search filing, and more.
All 11 languages complete.

string-array.name: changelog_v21
string-array.item: Home and list each get portrait and landscape two-column switches; paired rows stay level.
Haptic strength: off, light, medium, strong.
Pinch-to-resize icons is on by default; the strip-range preview scales its letters.
Home long-press can change the wallpaper.
The Frequent tag converges when the language changes; tag menus no longer double; the tag picker clears the status bar.
The changelog follows the language; tapping the app name opens the project page.

string-array.name: changelog_v20
string-array.item: Search finds apps by pinyin — initials and full spelling — with the match highlighted.
App tags group apps across the alphabet: sections on top, three letters in the strip, multi-select tagging with existing tags offered.
The Frequent tag follows usage on its own and can be switched off, taking its tags back; a hand-applied Frequent is refused.
A per-app lock asks for the screen lock, with a lock badge on the name; unlocking lifts a pause where the system allows.
The long-press menu gains uninstall; hiding an app asks first; paused apps grey out live.
Favorites reach the bottom edge like the app list and scroll fully into view, with room to spare.
Scrubbing past Z stays at Z; overscrolling the list bottom springs back instead of closing it.
The strip rests in the lower half (full height sideways); the palette picker is a five-column grid of flat Material colors.
Settings back navigation returns to the section it came from, system Back included; settings search finds every row.
Widgets refresh the moment their app freezes and unfreezes, and a frozen widget is never cleaned away.
Night dark theme, wallpaper blur, pinch-to-resize icons, reduced motion.
Backups now cover every setting including the language; private-space keys stay out of them.
About leads with the app name — tapping it opens the project page; the changelog follows the language.

string-array.name: changelog_v19
string-array.item: Language can now be chosen in settings — 10 languages plus Traditional Chinese.
The A-Z strip sits on the side the app list is not aligned to, and the launcher keeps you where you were when the language changes.
Home screen content no longer sits under the status bar when it is shown.
Set as default: a card on the home screen offers to make Deluge your home app, and can be dismissed for good.

string-array.name: changelog_first
string-array.item: Renamed and rebranded as Deluge Launcher, with a new blue theme and icon.
App list: runs edge to edge, and the strip lights up every letter on screen while scrolling.
Fixed scrolling — the list no longer refuses to scroll when a swipe starts at an angle.
Fixed the home screen being slow or blank for a couple of seconds when returning from another app.
Faster cold start: app icons are cached on disk.
Folder rows show how many apps they hold, and whether they are open.
Widgets: height follows the widget itself unless it is set by hand, and dead ones left over from a backup are cleaned up.
Swipe for shortcuts only fires on a sideways swipe, so scrolling past a row is never stolen.
Dropped the navigation library in favour of the launcher\'s own.
